explain.say: Here are tools for when you feel stuck. Take one slow breath. Do a tiny first step. Set a timer for 5 minutes. Or ask for help. Say, Can you help me start, please? Next time you feel stuck, pick one tool.

zones.label: Stuck
zones.note: It feels too big to start.

tools.label: Ask for help
tools.ask: What can I say when I am stuck?

faq.a: A big job can feel too much before you begin. Many people want to put it off. Once you start, the feeling usually gets smaller.
asks: Tell me about It feels too big

faq.a: A tiny start is the smallest first bit, like writing your name, or doing just one sum. It gets you moving.
asks: Tell me about Just one sum
Tell me about Tiny first step

faq.q: What can I say when I am stuck?
faq.a: You can say, Can you help me start, please? or Can you do the first one with me? A grown-up you trust can help.
asks: Tell me about Ask for help

faq.q: How does a timer help me start?
faq.a: Set a timer for five minutes and say, I will only work until it rings. Five minutes feels small enough to begin.

faq.q: What if I still cannot start?
faq.a: That is okay. Take a short movement break, then try the tiny start again. Tell a grown-up how it feels.

facts: Breaking a job into a tiny first step is a common way to get started.
A slow breath out can help the body feel calmer.

quiz.say: Kofi's maths page feels too big. How can he begin?

options.show: Do the whole page at once

quiz.why: One sum is small enough to begin. Then the next one feels easier.

wrong.0: The whole page at once is the big job that feels too much.
wrong.1: Putting it away leaves the job waiting for later.

quiz.say: Aoife feels stuck on her homework. What can she say to a grown-up?
quiz.show: Aoife feels stuck. What can she say?

options.show: Can you help me start, please?
options.say: Can you help me start, please?

quiz.why: Asking for help is a good choice. A grown-up can do the first one with her.

wrong.1: Later, the job will still feel big, so asking now helps.
wrong.2: TV can come later, when the homework is done.
